sentences.text: Revenue rose from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025, a 34.8% compound annual rate [F1][F10][F196].
Net loss peaked at $3.45 billion in FY2017 [F32] and narrowed to $460.5 million in FY2025 [F40].
FY2017 revenue rose 104.0% [D36], but a $2.6 billion rise in stock-based compensation [P74] widened the loss to $3.45 billion [F32].
The FY2018 loss narrowed 63.5% [D82] to $1.26 billion [F33] as stock-based compensation fell $2.1 billion [P75].
Advertising revenue reached $5.19 billion in FY2025 [S39] and 87.4% of revenue [D536], but growth slowed from 11.2% [D534] to 5.8% [D537], adding 5.3pp of the 10.6% total growth [D538][D406].
Other revenue grew 62.9% to $745 million [D544][S42], adding 5.4pp [D545] and lifting its share to 12.6% [D543].
The filing attributes advertising growth to about 17% more impressions, partly offset by about 10% lower cost per impression, and other revenue growth to more subscribers [P24].
Operating expenses grew 5.1% [D423] against 10.6% revenue growth [D406], so the operating loss shrank 32.4% [D407] and the incremental margin was 44.8% [D429].
The per-share loss fell 35.7% [D409], more than the 34.0% drop in net loss [D408], because diluted shares rose 2.1% [D425].
Operating margin of -9.0% [F30] is the window high [D554], against a window median of -32.4% [D555] and low of -422.5% [D553].
At -9.0% [F30], the company ranks at the 0th percentile of five internet peers [D570], against a peer median of 20.3% [D571].
The 5.7pp improvement in FY2025 [D419] came from cost of revenue (1.1pp [D431]), R&D (1.3pp [D432]) and other lines (3.3pp [D433]).
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on lower marketing spend [P22], while G&A rose $60.0 million on legal and professional fees [P21] and R&D rose $101.9 million on product headcount [P23].
Other income of $68.9 million [X130], mainly $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains [P18], lifted net margin to -7.8% [F50], above the -9.0% operating margin [F30].
Free cash flow was $437 million in FY2025 [F100], a 7.4% margin [D393] and the window high [D560], while the net loss was $460.5 million [F40].
Operating cash flow of $656 million [F80] reflects the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $164 million of D&A [P13][X80].
The filing ties capex of $219 million [F90], 3.7% of revenue [D392] and 1.34x D&A [D395], to leased-facility improvements [P10].
Net cash was negative $596 million in FY2025 [D399], or -10.1% of revenue [D400], down from $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D211].
At -10.1% [D400], net cash to revenue ranks at the 0th percentile of five internet peers [D578], against a median of 45.0% [D579].
Cash and investments of $2.94 billion [D397] sit against $3.54 billion of total debt [D398]; the 3.56x current ratio [F180] is the window low [D565], against a 5.15x median [D567].
Debt was refinanced more than enlarged: the 2033 notes, $1.50 billion principal [P2], primarily funded repurchases of 2026 to 2028 notes for $1.4 billion [P1].
Diluted shares rose from 808 million in FY2016 [X141] to 1.69 billion in FY2025 [X150].
The company reported a net loss in every year from FY2016 to FY2025 [R1][F31][F40], and stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D390], at least 10% in nine years [R2].
Stock-based pay of $1.02 billion [X90] exceeds the $532 million operating loss [F20], so the reported loss is mainly an equity charge.
Net cash fell four years running, from $197 million in FY2022 [D256] to net debt of $596 million in FY2025 [D399] [R3].
Refinancing with the 2033 notes [P2] mainly moved maturities out, so the higher interest cost of $122 million, up from $21.6 million [X100][X99], is a lasting drag.
Buybacks of $751 million [X156] were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D402], after 544.3% in FY2023 [D307] and 142.3% in FY2024 [D354] [R4].
The filings cited do not explain these repurchases, so they were funded from a balance sheet already in net debt of $596 million [D399].
Operating margin in the FY2026 10-K below -9.0% [F30], the window high [D554], would reverse the FY2025 gain.
Net cash in the FY2026 10-K: a move back above -$205 million [D304] would show refinancing narrowing the gap, while a move below -$596 million [D399] would confirm the trend.
Buybacks above $437 million of free cash flow [F100], against $751 million in FY2025 [X156], would confirm the pattern in the FY2026 10-K; buybacks below it would show it has ended.
